one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent flattened and then permanently deleted the required pmars-0.9.4 source directory (steps 11-14), destroying the Debian source tree structure the verifier expects, and separately misidentified '-d' as the debugger flag instead of '-e', triggering a cascade of unnecessary Makefile changes including -DSERVER which explicitly disables the debugger.
t_err_evidence: Step 11: agent ran 'mv pmars-0.9.4/* /app/' which flattened the contents of pmars-0.9.4 into /app and left pmars-0.9.4 as an empty shell, destroying the required source directory structure. The verifier expects a pmars-* directory under /app containing the full source tree.
t_commit_evidence: Step 14: agent ran 'rm -rf pmars-0.9.4 *.tar.xz *.dsc flashpaper.red rave.red', permanently deleting the pmars-0.9.4 directory and the original .dsc/.tar.xz files needed to reconstruct it. After this point, there is no pmars-* source directory in /app and the agent never attempts to restore it via re-running apt-get source.
trigger_explanation: At step 10, the agent listed /app and saw pmars-0.9.4 alongside .red files and concluded it needed to 'move this to /app'. However it was already in /app. Without verifying the actual current working directory or understanding the directory was already correctly placed, the agent prematurely executed 'mv pmars-0.9.4/* /app/' which flattened the tree before properly analyzing whether the directory was already in the right place.
forewarning_evidence: Step 13: agent listed pmars-0.9.4/ and found it contained only '.pc' (an empty quilt directory), indicating the flatten operation had already corrupted the source structure. Step 10 analysis also notes 'State Understanding: no' because the agent thought files were in the wrong place when they were already in /app. Despite seeing the nested directory was empty, the agent proceeded to delete it at step 14 rather than restoring it.
